title: Case homes, sold homes and named groups compared, per resident day and per bed
question: Do the homes the nursing cases single out draw more complaints, findings or State action, for their size, than the other homes here?
finding: Per 1,000 resident days, 2023 to 2025 (allegations / distinct complaints and incidents / substantiated with deficiencies): case homes below the California middle on nurse hours 0.831 / 0.624 / 0.0693, other case homes 0.703 / 0.567 / 0.0416. Sold homes that are not case homes 0.985 / 0.701 / 0.081, case homes not sold 0.859 / 0.702 / 0.0663; State actions per 100 beds, 2023 to 2026: 2.09 and 2.4. Life Generations' four homes: 0.516 / 0.423 / 0.0232, 3 State actions, none of class AA or A.
how: Each group's rates are pooled: the sum of its complaints (or findings) over the sum of its resident days, and the sum of its tags, actions and penalties over the sum of its licensed beds. Measures as in chf-homes-by-size. Groups: the 42 homes of the related-balance case; the 22 of them below the California middle on nurse hours (health_more screen nursing-home-low-staff-related); homes with a federal change of ownership effective 2019 to 2024 in the six case counties (the owner's list, 47 homes); groups as named in each home's State report (health_records screen ltc-disclosure-where-profit-went).
limits: The groups overlap and are small; a single home with many reported incidents moves a group. Sold homes were chosen by sale, case homes by their balance sheets, so neither is a random sample of Bay Area homes, and neither group is a control for the other.
